key_insight: A wall-sensor neural estimator can be highly accurate offline yet still destabilize opposition control in closed loop because the controller changes the data distribution it must predict.
engineering_relevance: For drag-reduction systems, sensor reconstruction must be dynamically consistent under feedback, not just accurate on prerecorded or fixed-flow data.
method: Train a recurrent estimator to infer near-wall detection-plane velocity from the two wall-shear-stress components.
Deploy it inside opposition control and compare offline reconstruction with live closed-loop behavior.
Stabilize wall-only control using spectral consistency in actuation and retraining on closed-loop data.
evidence_signal: The estimator reaches 0.99 correlation and near-unity coherence offline, but in closed loop it decorrelates within a few viscous time units as control collapses.
watch_item: Low-pass filtering and exponential averaging may delay failure but do not fix the underlying distribution-shift instability.
paper_title: Offline accuracy is not enough: closed-loop instability and stabilisation of a wall-sensor neural estimator in opposition control
